doc.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Claude Hopkins radio broadcasts and Edmond Hall
summary: Edmond Hall taught him; he idolised the Claude Hopkins band heard live from Roseland at noon.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yes. Well he was in “The Benny Goodman Story” with the Louis Armstrong band. As a matter of fact he was one of the ones who taught me how to play and how to act and all that kind of stuff. So I always wanted to be a singer and a trumpet player. There used to be, at twelve o’clock every day all over the country, there was a band called The Claude Hopkins Orchestra. And they came from the Roseland Ballroom at twelve o’clock. Now this was during the days when they didn’t have that many radio stations you know. Like ABC, CBS, NBC, and you could hear the Claude Hopkins band, and this guy would say,

“It’s twelve noon on Broadway,” and then you would hear Ovie Alston saying, “I will swim the ocean wide/I will take that great big ride.” And man I used to go crazy. I’d say this has got to be one of the days.
And they were probably playing live then too, right?
This wasn’t a record you were hearing, this was the real band.

No, no, no, this was Claude Hopkins Orchestra, which was supposed to be like against Duke Ellington’s band. As a matter of fact, the Roseland Ballroom, what I’d say, was one of the best jobs in the country, and it’s still running. Now I hope I’m not giving them a big plug, but the Roseland Ballroom is still alive on 52nd Street. Then one day I think my mother came up to New York vacationing, and she breaks out that her son was the greatest trumpet player in the world.
